findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral connector such as "Separately," or move the equipment-catalog fact into its own section.
findings.location: Program Overview, second paragraph ("Similarly, the IT asset group tracks...")
findings.violation: "Similarly" signals that this sentence parallels the one before it, but tracking the equipment catalog on a monthly cadence is a different subject and a different frequency than updating the reimbursement log at the start of the fiscal year, so the connector misrepresents the relationship between the two facts.

findings.evidence: "However, employees on an approved leave of absence remain eligible once they return to active status."
findings.fix: Replace "However" with "Additionally" or "Note that," since this sentence clarifies rather than contrasts.
findings.location: Eligibility, second paragraph ("However, employees on an approved leave of absence...")
findings.violation: "However" signals a contrast with the eligibility rule just stated, but returning from leave does not contradict the 90-day, one-claim rule, so the transition implies an exception where none actually exists.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person and name the actor, for example: "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition; the benefits team may request a photo check once a year."
findings.violation: Every other section refers to "employees" and "the employee" in third person, but this sentence switches to second person ("You" and "we"), breaking the document's voice and leaving "we" undefined as to whether it means the benefits team, finance, or IT.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Remove "Similarly" and state the rule as its own sentence, for example: "The policy also limits employees to one device per category."
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this rule parallels the equipment-condition rule just stated, but a per-category device limit is an unrelated restriction, so the connector obscures rather than clarifies the relationship between the two sentences.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Vary the phrasing after the first mention (for example "it" or "the item"), and convert "you record" to third person to match the rest of the document.
findings.violation: "The stipend item" is repeated verbatim three times across three consecutive sentences, and the paragraph continues the second-person "you" voice introduced earlier, so the passage reads as mechanically assembled rather than written for a reader.

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for this record throughout the document, or state explicitly that "request log" and "reimbursement log" are the same artifact.
findings.violation: "Request log" does not appear anywhere else in the document; Program Overview instead names a "reimbursement log" maintained by the IT asset group, leaving it unclear whether these refer to the same record under two different names.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either list the complete sequence of steps here, or remove this section and direct the reader to How to Apply as the authoritative process description.
findings.violation: This section reduces the request process to two steps, but How to Apply and Required Documentation already describe a longer sequence, including the portal walkthrough, the autosaved draft, and the confirmation summary, so a reader cannot tell whether "Request Steps" is a complete process, a partial summary, or a different process altogether.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two statements into one consistent description of who maintains the catalog and how often, and rename this section if it is not actually describing a special case.
findings.violation: Program Overview already states that "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month," so this sentence conflicts with that one on both who owns the catalog and how often it is updated; the section heading "Special Cases" also does not describe any actual exception or edge case.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Combine these sections into a single description of the approval chain that names each party's role and the order in which they act.
findings.violation: This section assigns intake-to-payout ownership to "the benefits team," but Approval Timeline already assigns review to "the manager," and Review Responsibility later assigns review to "the finance office," without ever clarifying how the team, the manager, and the finance office relate to one another in the approval chain.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: State explicitly whether the finance office's review is additional to or a replacement for the manager's review, and cross-reference the Approval Timeline section.
findings.violation: This introduces a dollar-based review threshold that is never mentioned in Approval Timeline, which says only that "the manager reviews the request," so a reader cannot tell whether the finance office's review happens in addition to the manager's review for every request, or replaces it for requests above 200 dollars.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Consolidate all equipment-catalog ownership and cadence statements into the Program Overview section, and rename this section to reflect its actual content, for example "Requesting a Printed Catalog."
findings.violation: This is a third, distinct claim about who maintains or reviews the equipment catalog and when, after the IT asset group's monthly tracking in Program Overview and the finance liaison's fiscal-year publication in Special Cases, and the heading "Questions and Updates" does not otherwise contain any questions or an update log.
